newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Edip Iplik to raise 1997 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Edip Iplik to raise 1997 turnover.

text.p: Turkish yarn producer Edip Iplik Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. plans to increase its turnover by 40 percent to 70 million DM in 1997, from approximately 50 million DM in 1996, a senior company official said.

"Our capacity expanding investments in 1996 and 1997 will help us to increase our turnover by 70 percent in two years to 85 million DM in 1998 over last year's 50 million DM," Kenan Koc, deputy general manager of the company, told Reuters.
Koc said the 1996 turnover was approximately 3.5 trillion lira and net profits were between 350-400 bllion lira, in line with previous projections.
Company shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange ended at 13,750 lira on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's 13,250.
"Our turnover will be 70 million DM in 1997, because the production in the new plants will begin in two stages, in April and July," he added.
The new investment will be effective on the balance sheet through nine and six months of the year.

Edip Iplik invested $10 million in 1996 on a new plant in Luleburgaz in northwestern Turkey to increase its sewing yarn production capacity by 1,000 percent to 2,200 kilograms per day from current 200 kilograms.
The company raised its paint-works capacity to 15 tonnes per day from five tonnes per day by installing new units at the new plant.

It plans to move 15,000 of its total 50,000 spindles to the new plant from its Istanbul plant this year. Koc said they would spend another seven million dollars in 1997 to have the new plant ready for operations.
The company will start a $2.5 million investment in 1998 to build a power co-generation plant near the Luleburgaz plant.
"The 4.5 megawat natural gas-based plant will meet 95 percent of our electricity demand in the new plant," Koc said.
"When we move all our production to the new plant, we will have to make another $2.5 million investment to expand out power units to meet all of our electricity and steam needs," he added.
The company would move its Istanbul facilities to Luleburgaz in three years at the earliest and in 10 years at the latest.
"But if anyone makes a good offer to buy the land where our current plant is, it would take us as short as 1-1/2 years to empty the area," he said.
The Istanbul plant, once located on the outskirts of the city, is now in the centre of a dense trade and business area where Turkey's major media groups are based.

The company reported 2.43 trillion lira turnover in the first nine months of 1996, against 1.44 trillion lira in the same period of 1995. Its net profit remained almost unchaged at 290 billion lira, versus 289 billion lira.
